video_title: Russell Westbrook Retires: Best Stories From A Hall Of Fame Career

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Russell Westbrook's Hall of Fame status in Oklahoma City
quotes.excerpt: Russ was a first ballot Hall of Famer before he ever left Oklahoma City.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: One of the most entertaining players and personalities that we've covered.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Russ was a first ballot Hall of Famer before he ever left Oklahoma City. If you just take the OKC portion of his career, it's first ballot Hall of Fame.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Russell Westbrook's refusal to adapt and evolve
quotes.excerpt: A lot of that stuff is his refusal to evolve, his refusal to adapt.
quotes.quote: The complications clouded the end of his career. There's a reason, Ramona, you wrote the story about his time in Denver, which went great for about a half season and then his welcome got worn out real quick. A lot of that stuff is his refusal to evolve, his refusal to adapt. There are a few superstars who adapt to different roles throughout the course of their career. Vince Carter is one who did and played a long time because of it. Russ very proudly refused to adapt. None of it diminishes what he did in Oklahoma City where Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is probably surpassing him at this point in delivered championships. As great as Kevin Durant is, Russell Westbrook is going to be considered no less than the second best player in franchise history.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Russell Westbrook's complex relationship with the media
quotes.excerpt: Russ didn't like the media, okay, that's not a secret, but Tim could take it.

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: Sam's interactions with Westbrook in that locker room, I got to tell you, that was one of my favorite things to just be a spectator for. Russ didn't like the media, okay, that's not a secret, but Tim could take it, he could give it, Russ appreciated that. He loved sparring with Tim McMahon.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: There's many players who have been like that over the decades.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Russell Westbrook's pursuit of the triple-double record
quotes.excerpt: I took that whole trip and it was when he was on the verge of breaking the triple-double record.
quotes.quote: I took that whole trip and it was when he was on the verge of breaking the triple-double record. I took it because our former colleague, Royce Young, had some unfortunate family circumstances so they needed me to fill in for him. This trip started in Memphis and Russ, off the top of my head, I want to say he ended up with 45 points, 13 assists, and 9 rebounds. He had one of many, many, many just unbelievable clutch closes where he had a clutch flurry of scoring, brought them back, incredible comeback win, but he was a rebound short of the triple-double. So he does his media and I didn't know Russ real well at the time, but I went up to him after his scrum broke up and I said, 'Hey Russ, I'm going to be on this trip, just want to let you know you'll be seeing me on the duration of this trip.' He said, 'Okay, cool.' I said, 'And John Reed, who is standing right next to me, he's one of the Thunder PR guys, John Reed said that we could sit down for an hour in Phoenix.'

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Tony's decision to play small ball in Houston
quotes.excerpt: Dan Tony in large part to benefit Russ said, 'Screw it, we're not going to play a center period.'
quotes.quote: He went there because James Harden wanted him there. He wanted a team with Harden and then the chemistry was weird. That's you also, the Dan Tony in large part to benefit Russ said, 'Screw it, we're not going to play a center period.' They traded Capela, they cut this young big named Isaiah Hartenstein, by the way, at the time. PJ Tucker is 6'5 played center for them and they won a lot of games and Russ put up some incredible numbers and then asked for a trade after the season and they shipped him to Washington where he put up great numbers for the Wizards.
